en: The Questions of Milinda:
The Chapter on Vessantara, Concerning the Question of Inference.
7. The Question on the Miracle at the Shrine “Venerable Nāgasena, does a miracle occur at the shrine for all those who have attained final nibbāna, or only for some?
“For some, Great King, it occurs; for others, it does not.”
“Venerable sir, for whom does it happen, and for whom does it not happen?
“Great king, for one of three kinds who has attained final nibbāna through a specific resolve, a miracle occurs at the stupa.
For which three? [The Buddha continued:]”
In this case, Great King, an Arahant, out of compassion for gods and humans, while still remaining in the world, resolves:

“Let a miracle occur at such-and-such a shrine. By virtue of that resolution, a miracle occurs at the shrine; in the same way, by virtue of the resolution of an Arahant who has attained final Nibbāna, a miracle occurs at his shrine.
Furthermore, Great King, out of compassion for human beings, deities display miracles at the stupa of one who has attained final Nibbāna, thinking:
‘By this miracle, the True Dhamma will be constantly upheld, and humans, being inspired with faith, will increase in wholesome states.
Thus, by way of the resolve of the deities, a miracle occurs at the stupa of one who has attained final Nibbāna.
Furthermore, Great King, suppose a woman or a man— faithful, confident, wise, competent, intelligent,
and endowed with discernment— having reflected wisely, places a perfume, a garland, a cloth,

or some other object upon a cetiya while resolving, ‘May it be thus named! Even for that which has been resolved upon for one who has attained final Nibbāna, [the name persists] by virtue of that resolution.
A miracle occurs at a shrine; thus, by virtue of the resolve of human beings, a miracle occurs at the shrine of one who has attained final Nibbāna.
It is by virtue of the resolve of one or another of these three, O Great King, that a miracle occurs at the shrine of one who has attained final Nibbāna.
If, O Great King, they had no such resolve, then even for one whose taints are exhausted, who possesses the six supernormal powers, and who has attained mastery over the mind—

“Great King, even if no miracle occurs at the cetiya, or even if there is no miracle, having seen the conduct that is perfectly pure, one must have confidence, reach a conclusion, and believe: ‘This son of the Buddha has attained final Nibbāna.
“Excellent, Bhante Nāgasena! It is so; I accept it as you say.”
The seventh question: The Miracle at the Shrine.
